study.title: Orca, OpenRig and Herdr, and What None of Them Do
study.not_tested: anything across two machines; Codex or Pi agents; Orca's orchestration commands and automations; OpenRig's watchdog and host pairing.

capabilities.label: Agents keep running when you disconnect

orca.note: Has a headless runtime (orca serve). Not tested.

openrig.note: The seats survived a daemon restart because tmux owns them.

herdr.note: Herdr's core claim. Not tested by closing the client.

openrig.note: rig ps flagged needs-input on both seats.

herdr.note: Reported blocked about 4s after the prompt, with the rule it matched.

capabilities.label: Each task in its own git worktree

orca.note: One command made the worktree and started the agent; both branches passed their tests.

openrig.note: Both seats shared one checkout in the test.

herdr.note: herdr worktree create exists. Not tested.

orca.note: Orchestration runs, tasks, dispatch and gates. Not tested.

openrig.note: The builder handed off to the reviewer through the queue.

herdr.note: It has prompt and wait primitives, not a queue.

capabilities.label: Bring a stopped team back where it left off

orca.note: The site promises scrollback restored on restart. Not tested.

openrig.note: Teardown, restore, and the builder remembered its work.

herdr.note: The site says it resumes agent sessions after a restart. Not tested.

orca.note: SSH worktrees and paired Orca servers. Not tested.

openrig.note: A host registry with pairing. Not tested.

herdr.note: herdr machine add over SSH. Not tested.

orca.note: orca search exists, but returned 'disabled' on this install. One host only, by its own help text.

openrig.note: rig ask: grep over one rig's transcripts.

capabilities.label: Memory shared across tools and machines

orca.note: Search covers one host: 'There is no all-computers search.'

capabilities.label: A warning before parallel agents collide

orca.note: No conflict command in its 288-command CLI schema; a real conflict surfaced only at git merge.

capabilities.label: Placing work by machine capacity or model limits

orca.note: It shows usage and rate-limit resets. It doesn't place work by them.

openrig.note: Its roster recommends specialists; no capacity-aware placement found.

capabilities.label: One permission and audit policy for all three

openrig.note: Records posture; the harness enforces, 'never runtime enforcement.'

herdr.note: Its own model: panes run as you.

steps.title: Boot a team from YAML
steps.sub: a custom spec with two Claude Code seats
steps.text:
$ rig up .rigspec/rig.yaml --cwd lab
  import_rig: ok

Rig: 01M5Z6XK6XQQ2FXTZXQMMDSYHW
Dashboard: rig ui open
Status: completed
$ rig ps --nodes --rig lab
RIG                    SESSION                                LIFECYCLE   ACTIVITY          WORK   ATTN REASON
lab                    dev-build@lab                          run         needs-input x1    no     yes  permission_prompt
lab                    dev-review@lab                         run         needs-input x1    no     yes  permission_prompt
steps.represents: OpenRig booting the two-seat lab team from a YAML spec, then both seats waiting on a dialog

steps.title: Hand the builder one bounded task
steps.sub: the task description had a mistake in it: only one test was failing
steps.represents: The bug-fix task sent to the builder, including the mistaken 'two fail'

steps.title: The handoff goes through the queue
steps.sub: the builder routed it without being told how
steps.text:
$ rig queue list --destination dev-review@lab
    "state": "in-progress",
    "summary": "Review one-line slugify fix (strip leading/trailing dashes) so test_slug.py passes; tests untouched",
$ git diff slug.py
-    return s
+    return s.strip("-")
steps.represents: OpenRig's queue after the builder handed the fix to the reviewer, and the one-line diff

steps.title: An independent review
steps.sub: and it corrected the task description
steps.text:
⏺ The slugify fix passes review with no blocking findings. I've sent the verdict
  back to the build seat on the queue.
  What I checked:
  - The diff is one line. It changes slug.py so the function strips dashes from
    both ends of the slug. Interior dashes are kept.
  - The tests are untouched. Git shows no change to test_slug.py.
  - All three tests pass. I ran them directly with python3 because pytest isn't
    installed here, which matches what the builder said.
  - The builder's correction holds. Only the trim test was failing before the
    fix, not two tests.
steps.represents: The reviewer's verdict, including its correction of the task

steps.title: Tear the whole team down
steps.text:
$ rig down lab --snapshot
Before stopping 01M5Z6XK6XQQ2FXTZXQMMDSYHW: recorded agent sessions: dev-build@lab (activity: idle), dev-review@lab (activity: idle).
Rig 01M5Z6XK6XQQ2FXTZXQMMDSYHW stopped. 2 session(s) killed.
Snapshot: 01M5Z78PWNDSX2JM2K9ARR743K
To restore: rig up 'lab' --existing
$ tmux ls | grep lab
steps.represents: Tearing the lab team down with a snapshot, leaving no lab sessions in tmux

steps.title: Restore it, then ask what it remembers
steps.text:
$ rig restore 01M5Z78PWNDSX2JM2K9ARR743K --rig lab
Restore attempt id: 1025
Status: started
$ rig restore status 1025 --rig lab
Original verdict: fully_restored
$ rig send dev-build@lab 'Quick check, no tool calls needed: in one sentence, what did you fix earlier in this session, and what did the reviewer say?'
⏺ I made slugify strip leading and trailing dashes, a one-line change that makes
  all three tests pass without touching them, and the reviewer said it passes
  with no blocking findings, noting only that accented titles give broken slugs
  and all-punctuation titles give an empty slug, both of which predate the fix.
steps.represents: Restoring the team from the snapshot, and the builder recalling its earlier work

quotes.text: Herdr is where your coding agents live
Herdr doesn't wrap them or replace them
Herdr isn't an app you keep open
OpenRig is the Terraform for Coding Agents
A harness wraps a model. A rig wraps your harnesses.
OpenRig doesn't guarantee it can preserve or roll back these files, so back them up first
